Command: A priest shall not marry a chalalah
Summary: The command: A priest shall not marry a chalalah (Leviticus 21:7). A priest might not marry a woman profaned by a forbidden union, a chalalah, whose status would profane his seed.
Commandment: A priest shall not marry a chalalah.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The marriage rules guarded the priesthood's public holiness in a world where priests were public figures; they are not Christian marriage law, which is governed by creation and by the New Testament household commands (Matthew 19:3-9; Ephesians 5:22-33). The high priest's stricter rule — a virgin of his own people — is included here as the second half of the same law.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: for he is holy unto his God (Leviticus 21:7-8).
